To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a panel of 46 H2 class II alleles that covers 95 % (at least four alleles) of all HLA class II haplotypes in the world, and that we have developed 46 corresponding HLA class II transfectant cell lines that can be used to determine MHC class II restriction of T cell epitopes in vitro.
we have developed a panel of HLA class-II transfectants, representing 90 % of the population, to facilitate high throughput HLA restriction analysis.

we have developed a panel of HLA class-II transfectants that covers the HLA class II allelic variants expressed by 90 % of the world population and can be used to determine the MHC restriction of T cell epitopes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a strategy that allows rapid and unambiguous determination of HLA class-II restriction.
the development of a strategy to determine MHC class II restriction broadly applicable to the DR, DQ and DP loci.
developing a comprehensive strategy to determine HLAB class II restriction, which will be of great benefit to the T cell immunology field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this panel of cell lines can be utilized to determine HLA restriction for any T cell epitope, and is a powerful tool to determine HLA-restricted epitopes for vaccine design and development.
this panel of 46 HLAB* transfectants is a powerful tool for determining the HLA class II specificity of T cells and for the development of HLAB tetramer staining reagents.
we have developed a strategy to determine H2 class II restriction broadly and efficiently.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an HLA class II cell line panel that can be used for high throughput screening to determine HLA restriction and to facilitate the development of H-2 tetrameric staining.
we have generated a panel of 46 HLAB cell lines that will allow the determination of HLA class I restriction for a large proportion of individuals in the general population.
this panel of HLA class IIT cells is a valuable tool that can be used to identify the HLA restriction of a large panel of epitopes in an unambiguous manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a panel of HLA class I and II cell lines, representing the allelic variants most frequently encountered in a given population, can be used to determine HLA restriction in a rapid and unambiguous manner.
the use of HLA class I-transfected cell line panels to determine T cell epitope restriction is a powerful tool for immunological studies.
it is possible to assemble a panel of cell lines that can be used to determine the restriction specificity of a large proportion of the HLA alleles expressed in the population.
